claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for launch on a narrow aggregate-readiness basis, supported by documentation and post-launch monitoring, without treating the clinical coding assistant gap as a blocking material weakness.
decision_criteria: Use `compliant` only if admissible evidence shows the named-use-case limitation was either resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Use `suspicious` if aggregate evidence supports launch in part but a required disclosure/materiality predicate remains unresolved or the packet overclaims support.
Treat named customer commitments and named launch use cases as materiality triggers even if product labels the segment non-core or low-volume.
Do not let public governance guidance on documentation and monitoring override the specific internal disclosure policy for material limitations.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the clinical coding assistant gap must be disclosed for this launch.
Any approved risk-acceptance record covering this named launch use case before launch.
The actual launch disclosure or model-card language, if the limitation was disclosed.
Evidence that the clinical coding assistant gap was remediated or no longer misses target before certification.
Documentation of the two hospital revenue-cycle commitments sufficient to confirm scope and contractual relevance.
specific_concerns: Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch readiness, but they do not resolve the separate policy question of material weakness disclosure for a named launch use case.
Admissible evidence says the underperforming clinical coding assistant segment is named in two hospital revenue-cycle commitments, which directly triggers the stated materiality policy.
The product note's 6% first-month traffic argument does not address the named contractual commitments and therefore does not resolve materiality under the policy text.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.

No admissible evidence shows the limitation was resolved before launch or covered by an approved risk acceptance, both of which the release policy identifies as the path to proceed without disclosure.
unsupported_claims: That certification is policy-compliant as presented, rather than merely operationally supportable on aggregate metrics.
Any implication that the segment gap is immaterial based on low projected traffic.
Any implication that documentation and monitoring commitments substitute for required disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance for a named launch use case.
